newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tremor shakes central Japan, no damage reported.
newsitem.headline: Tremor shakes central Japan, no damage reported.

text.p: A strong earthquake shook a wide area of central Japan on Sunday, rattling office buildings in Tokyo and forcing the suspension of bullet train service on a section of the country's east coast, authorities said.
There were no immediate reports of damage and authorities said there was no danger of "tsunami" tidal waves.
The earthquake at 2:51 p.m. (0551 GMT) measured 5.6 on the Richter scale with its epicentre in Aichi prefecture, about 250 km (150 miles) southwest of Tokyo, the Meteorological Agency said.

At least 11 prefectures in the central part of the main island of Honshu experienced moderate to strong tremors from the earthquake, which shook office buildings in central Tokyo for about 10 seconds.
Earlier this week, authorities said seismic activity had subsided after about 9,000 mostly minor tremors had shaken the coastal resort area of Ito, about 130 km (78 miles) southwest of Tokyo.
